title: Dumbbell Fly
summary: A fly with dumbbells on a flat bench that stretches the chest hard at the bottom.

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for chest (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly chest total.
Library rating 0.3 for front delts (minor): each working set adds 0.3 of a set to the weekly front delts total.

setup.text: Lie on a bench with the dumbbells over your chest and your palms facing each other.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and lower the weights out to the sides in an arc.
Stop when you feel a strong chest stretch, usually with your upper arms about level with the bench.
Bring them back up along the same arc.

form_cues.cue: Keep a soft bend in the elbows
Lower in a wide arc to a chest stretch
Bring the bells back up over your chest
Go lighter than you think. The stretch at the bottom is where your shoulders are most exposed.

mistakes.text: Turning it into a press by bending the elbows more as the weights come up.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds no ramp-up sets; make the first working set a touch lighter if you like.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 10% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 10-15 reps, stopping about 2 reps short of failure (RIR 2). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train pain-free.

alternatives.why: Swap sheet: Better isolation, More stable, Steadier cable tension.
Swap sheet: Lower-chest bias, Better isolation, More stable.
Swap sheet: Less stretch emphasis, Peak-contraction focus, Better isolation.
